title: FinEval-KR: A Financial Domain Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models' Knowledge and Reasoning

model.params_source: paper Sec. 5.3 (temperature 1, three independent runs); o3-mini ignores temperature, reasoning_effort not stated (API default medium assumed); max_completion_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: all released items (the repository provides a 625-instance sample covering the 22 subfields; the paper's set has 9,782 questions), three runs each
task.approximation: Only the 625-item public sample is available instead of the full 9,782 questions (set-level comparison at best); the judge is self-hosted Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct; reasoning effort unstated.

items.source: https://github.com/SUFE-AIFLM-Lab/FinEval-KR (22 per-subfield JSONL files, 625 instances in total)

fields.label: gt (reference step-by-step solution and final answer)

prompt.source_location: Appendix F, Figure 15 (Stage 1 prompt template, original Chinese with English translation: 'You are a financial expert, and you need to answer the following question in Chinese and provide the complete solution process. Please think step-by-step, and only consider the scenario described in the problem during the solution process; do not add extra information. Question: {Given Financial Reasoning Problem}')

output.parse: free text (unconstrained solution); correctness decided by the judge

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: Acc = share of questions whose Stage-1 solution the judge marks as reaching the correct final answer (Sec. 4.2.1 / Eq. for Acc), averaged over the three runs.
metric.judge: llm:Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (self-hosted), prompt location Appendix F, Figure 14 (structured CoT judge prompt, Chinese)
metric.original_location: Table 3, row o3-mini, column Acc (std in Table 7)

open_points: The judge is a self-hosted Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct with the Figure 14 CoT prompt; the battery calls OpenAI models only, so the judge stage cannot run inside the runner (aux model not callable).
The public release holds 625 of the 9,782 evaluation questions; a 625-item set-level comparison must be accepted before spending.
notes: The three runs are the paper's protocol (mean reported), counted in est_calls; a full 9,782-question run would be ~29k calls (~USD 450). || [hook pass 2026-09-07] no hook: judge model not callable through the battery.
